description: Number of vCPUs to expose to the guest. Range 1..32 (Firecracker design cap). Each vCPU runs in its own KVM_RUN-loop thread.
Guest RAM size in mebibytes. Backed by anonymous host memory (or hugepages, see huge_pages). Snapshot mem_file_path is this size.
x86-only. Whether to expose Intel hyperthreading siblings to the guest's CPUID. Default false to avoid side-channel concerns; production deployments typically keep this off.
Enable KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES on the guest RAM region. REQUIRED for diff snapshots — without it, only Full snapshots are possible. Slight runtime overhead from dirty-bit page-walk on KVM exit.
Back guest RAM with hugepages — None (4KiB) or 2M (2MiB hugepages). 2M reduces TLB pressure for large guests but requires reserved hugepages on the host (vm.nr_hugepages sysctl).
DEPRECATED. Static CPU template (None|T2|T2A|T2CL|T2S|C3|V1N1). Use PUT /cpu-config for custom templates instead. Affects CPUID + MSR exposure for snapshot portability.
Host filesystem path to an uncompressed Linux kernel (ELF on x86, PE on aarch64). Firecracker does not provide a kernel; user supplies one built per fc-docs-rootfs-kernel.md.

Linux command line passed to the guest kernel. Common additions: console=ttyS0 (serial console output), root=/dev/vda (boot disk), ip=... (static IP). Firecracker validates basic syntax but doesn't constrain content.
Optional initramfs file. Loaded into guest memory before kernel boot.
Block-device cache mode. Unsafe = drop guest flush requests (faster, but data loss on crash). Writeback = honor flush (correct, slightly slower). Use Writeback for any non-ephemeral data.
Block I/O backend. Sync = read/write syscalls. Async = io_uring (kernel >=5.10) for better throughput on high IOPS workloads.
Token bucket controlling bandwidth (bytes). size = bucket capacity, refill_time = ms to refill, one_time_burst = optional one-shot extra capacity.
Token bucket controlling I/O operations per second. Independent of bandwidth bucket.
Log verbosity: Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Trace. Trace adds significant overhead; Debug is the practical-max for production.
Prepend each log line with source-file:line. Useful for debugging Firecracker itself; usually off in production for log volume.
MMDS protocol version. V1 = unauthenticated GET (legacy). V2 = session-token-required (PUT to get token, then GET with token header). V2 mimics EC2 IMDSv2 and is recommended for SSRF protection.
Guest-side IPv4 address that resolves to MMDS. Default matches EC2 IMDS for compatibility with cloud-init and other guest tooling.

How guest RAM is materialized during restore. File = read snapshot mem file into anonymous memory (eager load). Uffd = userfaultfd-backed lazy load — pages copied on first guest access (lower memory footprint, slightly higher first-access latency).
